top.title: Rivers crisis: You’ll not regret choosing peace, Tinubu assures Fubara
top.description: By Ayobami Okerinde President Bola Tinubu has assured Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, that he would not regret his decision to embrace peace and respect the intervention of political elders in resolving the crisis that rocked the state. Tinubu gave the assurance on Saturday while addressing supporters at the All Progressives Congress, APC, 2027 presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt. He said, “To me, I intervened on your behalf. Similarly, to Fubara, Your Excellency, the host governor of today, I want to thank you specifically for maturity, understanding, respect for the wisdom of elders. “When we intervened, you respected our position. You maintained peace. You are a committed democrat, Fubara. You will not regret what you have done as long as all of us are alive,” Tinubu said. The political crisis, which erupted in October 2023, followed a breakdown in relations between Fubara and his predecessor, now Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, over control of the state’s political structure. The crisis escalated in March 2025 when Tinubu declared a state of emergency in the state , suspending Fubara, his deputy, Ngozi Odu, and members of the House of Assembly for six months. Fubara returned to office in September 2025 following the expiration of the emergency rule. However, political tensions resurfaced, with lawmakers initiating another impeachment process against him and his deputy in January 2026. Efforts to reconcile the feuding camps gained momentum in June 2025 when Tinubu convened a meeting involving Fubara, Wike and members of the Rivers State House of Assembly at the Presidential Villa in Abuja. More recently, in October , Fubara and Wike held another reconciliation meeting in Port Harcourt alongside their supporters, in what was seen as an effort to consolidate the rapprochement between the two political camps. top.title: Penn State football injury issues at wide receiver vs Washington
top.description: SEATTLE — Penn State football appears to be getting healthy at most every place on its roster for the stretch drive, in order to best save whatever it can of a second straight disappointing season. To start by building momentum and positivity for its cross-country adventure here on Saturday, Nov. 7, in Washington's Husky Stadium . Getting healthy most everywhere except for their rebuilt receiver room. While senior Chase Sowell appears to be returning from injury against the Huskies , sophomore sensation Koby Howard will miss his sixth straight game with an undisclosed injury, according to the latest Big Ten availability report . Meanwhile, freshman wideout Zay Robinson was listed as "questionable" all week and will be a "game-time decision" against the Huskies. Robinson also has excelled as the Lions' primary kickoff and punt returner. Other game-time decisions include starting offensive tackle Malachi Goodman and top backup defensive tackle Armstrong Nnodim. This means the Lions' viable receiving options Saturday could be down to Sowell, junior transfer Brett Eskildsen and true freshman Amarion Jackson. Eskildsen, one of the fastest players on the team, is averaging only 30.5 yards per game on his 23 receptions this season. Rather, the Lions and quarterback Rocco Becht may lean, again, on their tight end room that finally appears fully healthy, particularly standout blocker and possession receiver Gabe Burkle, who has been working his way back from knee surgery last fall. Otherwise, the Lions appear in better shape, physically, for Washington and the final three games than they have for most of the season. Penn State's list of unavailable players for the Washington game includes Howard, linebacker Alex Tatsch, defensive end Max Granville , cornerback Tyler Armstead, defensive tackle Alijah Carnell and kickoff specialist Cristiano Rosa . top.title: Tuipulotu takes 'full responsibility' for Scotland collapse
top.description: Captain Sione Tuipulotu took responsibility for Scotland's second-half Nations Championship collapse against New Zealand, saying they were "nowhere near accurate enough". Trailing by just three points at half-time, Scotland were well in the contest as they sought a first victory against the All Blacks at the 34th attempt. However, they failed to score any points in the second half as New Zealand swept to a clinical 43-21 victory at Murrayfield. Tuipulotu was sin-binned on 50 minutes after a succession of penalties went against the Scots and they were unable to wrestle back momentum from there. "Disappointing," was Tuipulotu's one-word review post-match. He added: "We played our rugby in the first half but we probably left points out there. We were nowhere near accurate enough second half, and we couldn't stick with them, it's really disappointing. "Our discipline wasn't good enough, and it starts with me. I got sent to the bin and 10 minutes with your captain off isn't good for any team. I take full responsibility for that." New Zealand cruise to victory as Scotland fade All the Scottish rugby latest in one place Scotland conceded 13 penalties to New Zealand's eight. Just moments after Tuipulotu went to the bin, Beauden Barrett cruised over to score his second and New Zealand's sixth try of the day. Game over. "First half we were playing our rugby, putting them under pressure with ball in hand, in a way they haven't been put under pressure over the past couple of weeks," Tuipulotu said. "We just weren't accurate enough when we got down into the 22m. We had lots of opportunities in the first half and weren't accurate enough in the second. "We know what we can do with ball in hand, which proves we weren't up to the level that the All Blacks were playing in the second half. "It's a must-win game [against Australia] next week, we'll regroup and stick together like we always do." In the first half, Scotland's maul and New Zealand's indiscipline kept the hosts in touch. After the interval, the All Blacks tightened up defensively and scored three magnificent tries. "Scotland kept getting the wrong side of Andrew Brace with Sione Tuiputotu going to the sin-bin," former Scotland captain John Barclay said on STV. "But the difference is red zone efficiency - when the team gets into the opposition 22m, how often do they score? New Zealand were at 58%, Scotland were at 30%. "There's a couple moments in the second half where they manage to get down into the 22m, and they lost the ball first phase. It's that clinical edge." top.title: Top 2027 recruit Ashley Maccalla commits to Rutgers
top.description: Top 2027 recruit Ashley MacCalla has committed to Rutgers over programs including Oklahoma, Miami and Cal. The 5-10 guard from Middletown (NY) St. James Performance Academy was one of the biggest stockrisers of the summer. “My biggest strength is that every time I step on a court, I’m one of the most athletic girls on the court,” she said. “I really take advantage of it, whether it’s on defense or offense, I’m the type of girl that plays in transition. I don’t really care about highlights or anything like that. I do what my team needs to win, whether that’s just playing defense, getting steals, getting blocks, or pushing in transition. I’m one of those girls that a coach will love to coach, because I don’t really care about the highlight reel and stuff like that. I just want to do what the team needs to do to win.” Rutgers was one of the more recent teams to enter her recruitment, but her relationships with the staff were central. “Rutgers has been on me a lot too, just because they’re literally an hour away from me,” she previously told Rivals. “It’s been really good. Coach G[ary Redus] met most of my family. He was recruiting me at LSU, so I talked to him a lot. I also talk a lot with Lauren Hansen. She used to play for Exodus and she coaches for Exodus for a little bit too, so I already had that bond with her and it’s great talking to them. My parents love him and he’s a great guy. He loves to talk. Campus is beautiful too.” There were several factors that went into her decision. “A connection with the coaches,” she said of important factors. “I’d say play style, like how I’d fit in the system and making sure I get a good opportunity to play. I also have an older sister and I want to make sure that she’s able to come with me. Also somewhere that I can develop. I want to make it to the league.”

top.title: Swans boss Matos defends Stamenic over red card
top.description: Swansea had been the more threatening side at Birmingham until Marko Stamenic (right) was sent off [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Vitor Matos has defended Marko Stamenic after the midfielder was sent off during Swansea City's defeat at Birmingham City. Stamenic saw red in the 26th minute for a heavy challenge on Ethan Laird. Birmingham seized the initiative after Stamenic's early exit, with Jay Stansfield swiftly putting the Blues ahead and then netting a late winner after Swansea levelled in the second half. Matos suggested Stamenic should not have been dismissed because he played the ball rather than former Swansea loanee Laird. "I cannot change what the referee decided," said the Swansea head coach. "I think what happened in that situation was that Marko touched the ball. He tackled the ball with the first foot, he tackled the ball with the second foot. "There's no contact between the two players, so then it's the judgement of the ref if that's a red or not. It's up to him not me." Birmingham beat 10-man Swansea to go top of table Stamenic faces a three-match ban after the first sending off of his Swansea career, with Birmingham boss Chris Davies describing the red card incident as "a poor challenge". Unless Swansea launch a successful appeal, New Zealand player Stamenic will miss games against West Brom, Middlesbrough and Cardiff City after the upcoming international break. "I am here already [in English football] for a good amount of time - I was here before," Matos added. "I saw so many challenges worse than this in the last game. Some of these challenges end up with players injured. It's just harsh when we have this challenge and then there's a red card. "It's for the refs to judge and try to find an agreement on where the line is." top.title: NASCAR CEO O’Donnell Bets On YouTube To Fix TV Ratings
top.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell delivered a blunt truth to the sports world on Friday at Homestead-Miami Speedway. While television ratings for the Cup Series are sagging, the front office refuses to panic. O’Donnell argues that the old metrics do not tell the whole story anymore. He pointed to a 5 percent rise in track admissions and a 12 percent jump in kids under 12 showing up to races, per Newsday . The sport is shifting its focus from the couch to the digital feed, betting that new fans will find the action online first. This is a bold gamble for a league built on tradition, but the numbers back the move. Digital First Strategy O’Donnell knows that a fan in New York or Seattle cannot drive to a race every weekend. The solution is to meet them where they live. “If you’re in New York or you’re in Seattle, and you don’t have a race, what is that entry point?,” O’Donnell said Friday. The answer is short clips and influencer content. To expand the series past its southern origins and enter international markets, the sanctioning body is leveraging YouTube and social media influencers. This strategy acknowledges that the path to a ticket starts with a viral moment on a phone screen. While critics might focus on the drop in broadcast viewership, the CEO sees a different picture. NBC viewership for last week’s Cup race at Martinsville Speedway was down 15 percent from last year, according to Newsday. With an average of just under 2 million viewers, that event became the least-watched non-delayed Cup race on broadcast television. Yet, O’Donnell insists that social impressions increased 34 percent year-over-year. Since 2013, interest levels among adults ages 18 to 34 have reached their peak. The sport is not dying; it is just changing how it breathes. Sponsor Money Talks Money flows to where the attention is, and NASCAR is seeing fresh cash. “Fans are coming out to the racetrack. New brands are investing in the sport like never before,” O’Donnell said. The activation from sponsors around teams and drivers is at a high point not seen in years. This spending power proves that brands believe in the future of the sport even if cable TV numbers dip. “It’s been a long time since you’ve seen the activation from sponsors around our teams and drivers,” O’Donnell noted. The league is also celebrating the addition of Dodge as a fourth manufacturer, adding more competition and buzz to the garage. O’Donnell pushed back hard against the narrative that NASCAR is struggling. “If you compared NASCAR to a new sport that’s just emerging you’d say it’s an incredible success story,” he said. The league has maintained a consistently large television audience across 36 straight weekends. top.description: Motorsport photo Ryo Hirakawa is unsure whether even bold strategic calls will be enough to propel Toyota towards the front in the World Endurance Championship's Monza finale after a difficult qualifying session. Hirakawa admitted the Japanese manufacturer was simply “too slow” after the two TR010 Hybrids ended up 15th and 16th on the grid for Sunday’s race, only ahead of the #15 BMW M Hybrid V8 of Dries Vanthoor. Teams had completed very little representative running on slick tyres across the three practice sessions, with persistent rain on Friday and Saturday morning severely compromising preparations for the Monza 6 Hours. However, Toyota struggled for performance in both wet and dry conditions as the WEC returned to Monza for the first time since the #7 crew's victory in 2023. “It was the same for everyone, no dry running until qualifying, so it was really tricky. Some cars had tested here; we hadn't, so we were just guessing for set-up. We did our best from what we have got, but it's been tough,” Hirakawa said, “Even in the wet, we didn't have a really strong pace.” Asked where he was losing time on track, Hirakawa replied: “In the wet, it was everywhere, even on the straights, but I haven't really seen the performance in the dry. Arteta praises Madueke's elite mentality Reflecting on the player's recent rise, Arteta said: 'He's a great example for the rest of the group because before the first international break he wasn't playing. top.title: Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton set for blockbuster rematch in final of Paris Masters
top.description: Carlos Alcaraz set up a rematch with US Open conqueror Ben Shelton after he eased into a maiden Paris Masters final with a 6-4 6-4 victory over Casper Ruud . Seven-time grand slam champion Alcaraz lost out in an epic to Shelton at Flushing Meadow in September on his comeback from a four-month lay-off with a wrist injury. The world number three has returned to the winners’ circle twice since his exit in the early hours in New York, but will aim to gain revenge on Shelton and secure another ATP 1000 title on Sunday. US Open runner-up Shelton got the better of home favourite Luca Van Assche by a 5-7 6-3 6-4 score at the start of the day. Carlos Alcaraz set up a meeting with Ben Shelton after a straight set win over Casper Ruud in Paris (Getty) After Shelton’s two-hour-and-17-minute battle, all eyes in Paris were on Alcaraz, who saved two match points to defeat Taylor Fritz on Friday. Ruud narrowly held off Alcaraz in two of his first three service games before the Spaniard broke to move 4-3 up and closed out the first set with a 130mph ace. The second stayed on serve until Alcaraz picked the opportune moment to break to go 5-4 ahead and secured victory inside 97 minutes. It made it eight wins in a row for Alcaraz, who reached an 11th Masters final, but first in Paris. Ben Shelton defeated Luca van Assche to reach Paris Masters Open (Reuters) “This tournament has always been really tough for me. I’ve struggled every time,” Alcaraz said on court. “I’ve come into this part of the season much fresher, hungry, ambitious, excited about coming to the tournaments and stepping on the court, playing matches and competing. I’m just really happy that I made the final.” Shelton, meanwhile, reached the final when he rallied from a break down in the deciding set to beat Van Assche on Saturday. The third-seeded American looked in trouble when the unseeded Frenchman broke his serve for a 3-1 lead in the third set. But Shelton responded by winning the next four games to lead 5-3. “I know there is always going to be some little chance I can execute,” Shelton said. “If I can be brave and keep winning my serve and stick with the guy, I feel there is a small window.”

top.title: Toto Wolff doesn’t think Kimi Antonelli “would have lasted in other teams”
top.description: Motorsport photo Formula 1 is a vicious meat grinder for young talent. If a rookie doesn't perform immediately, there is usually a very short leash before a team principal shows them the door. For Mercedes , taking a massive gamble on teenager Andrea Kimi Antonelli to replace Lewis Hamilton was the ultimate risk. And as team boss Toto Wolff freely admits, there was a dark stretch during the Italian's 2025 rookie campaign where almost any other team on the grid would have pulled the plug. Speaking to Sky Sports F1’s Naomi Schiff and Simon Lazenby following Free Practice 3 at the Brazilian Grand Prix, Wolff took a moment to reflect on exactly how close his newly crowned world champion came to the brink. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Before Antonelli hoisted the 2026 championship trophy in Mexico City, he had to survive a nightmare slump. "What I'm particularly proud of is that I don't think he would have lasted in other teams after an F2 season, which wasn't overwhelming," Wolff confessed on the Sky broadcast. "And this spell of nine races without any points last year." The Mercedes shield When the pressure was at its absolute peak, and critics were questioning the factory seat, the Brackley squad closed ranks. They ignored the outside noise and looked at the telemetry. "We just trusted our data, trusted our feeling about the personality and the potential," Wolff explained. "Because there's so many that came out and said, what a talent. And that wasn't the journey." Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes Instead of letting the then-19-year-old drown in the immense pressure of the Silver Arrows spotlight, Wolff and his senior leadership team built a psychological fortress around him. They gave him the time that other teams simply refuse to offer. "The journey was developing the talent, nurturing, mentoring, shielding him, protecting him," Wolff noted. "And eventually, you know, he in the car is just delivered absolutely amazingly." The ultimate vindication arrived in Mexico when Antonelli secured the crown. Wolff's patience didn't just save a generational talent from being destroyed by the F1 machine - it built the youngest world champion in F1 history. nigeria.title: Rivers crisis: You’ll not regret choosing peace, Tinubu assures Fubara
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde President Bola Tinubu has assured Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, that he would not regret his decision to embrace peace and respect the intervention of political elders in resolving the crisis that rocked the state. Tinubu gave the assurance on Saturday while addressing supporters at the All Progressives Congress, APC, 2027 presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt. He said, “To me, I intervened on your behalf. Similarly, to Fubara, Your Excellency, the host governor of today, I want to thank you specifically for maturity, understanding, respect for the wisdom of elders. “When we intervened, you respected our position. You maintained peace. You are a committed democrat, Fubara. You will not regret what you have done as long as all of us are alive,” Tinubu said. The political crisis, which erupted in October 2023, followed a breakdown in relations between Fubara and his predecessor, now Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, over control of the state’s political structure. The crisis escalated in March 2025 when Tinubu declared a state of emergency in the state , suspending Fubara, his deputy, Ngozi Odu, and members of the House of Assembly for six months. Fubara returned to office in September 2025 following the expiration of the emergency rule. However, political tensions resurfaced, with lawmakers initiating another impeachment process against him and his deputy in January 2026. Efforts to reconcile the feuding camps gained momentum in June 2025 when Tinubu convened a meeting involving Fubara, Wike and members of the Rivers State House of Assembly at the Presidential Villa in Abuja. More recently, in October , Fubara and Wike held another reconciliation meeting in Port Harcourt alongside their supporters, in what was seen as an effort to consolidate the rapprochement between the two political camps. nigeria.title: Arsenal edge past Hull to stretch Premier League lead
nigeria.description: Arsenal beat stubborn Hull 1-0 to stretch their lead at the top of the Premier League to six points on Saturday while Tottenham’s recent revival was halted at Leeds. Mikel Arteta’s Gunners were strongly tipped to get the better of the visitors, who have not won in the league since August, but were made to sweat despite dominating the match. Captain Martin Odegaard finally broke the deadlock for the champions and title favourites in the 72nd minute to give Arsenal their ninth win in 10 games. Manchester City can close the gap to three points if they beat struggling Nottingham Forest in the late kick-off as they seek to avoid a third straight defeat. Arsenal, who hogged possession at the Emirates, had a claim for a penalty in the closing minutes of the first half after Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy. But VAR ruled that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up. Frustration mounted as the second half unfolded but Odegaard came to Arsenal’s rescue, scoring his first goal since early September with a poacher’s finish. Noni Madueke cut in from the right before unleashing a left-footed shot that Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled, with Odegaard firing home from close range. – VAR controversy – In the early kick-off, Leeds struck in the 79th minute through substitute Noah Okafor to end Tottenham’s three-match winning run. The major talking point in the first half was a challenge by Leeds defender Jayden Bogle on Spurs winger Mathys Tel, which was reviewed for a potential red card by VAR officials before eventually being cleared. Tel had to leave the field shortly before half-time. Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, disappointed by his team’s second-half showing, refused to be drawn on the incident, which was not reviewed on the pitchside monitor by referee John Brooks. “In the first situation of Mathys Tel I didn’t see, I can’t say nothing,” he told TNT Sports after the 1-0 defeat. He added: “I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR and if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know, but we have confidence.” Defeat is a bitter blow for Spurs, who arrived at Elland Road in buoyant mood after recovering from a shocking start to the season. Leeds manager Daniel Farke said his team, who had been winless in five league games, had shown “great spirit, great commitment, great unity”. Elsewhere, Jacob Murphy put Newcastle on course for a much-needed win with a spectacular strike in the 80th minute at Craven Cottage but substitute Rodrigo Muniz levelled just three minutes later to earn a 1-1 draw. nigeria.title: Argentina FA to appeal World Cup final sanctions to CAS
nigeria.description: Argentina’s football association (AFA) announced on Saturday it had appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the sanctions FIFA imposed on it over World Cup final incidents. Midfielder Leandro Paredes was the hardest hit with a 10-game ban and $90,000 fine for his role in clashes with Spain players. He grabbed Eric Garcia by the throat and wrestled Gavi to the ground while holding his substitute’s bib, which led to an escalation in the incidents on the field after the final that Spain won 1-0 at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on July 19. The AFA was fined $321,000 for breaches of FIFA’s disciplinary code relating to using a sports event for making demonstrations of a non-sporting nature, team misconduct, and discriminatory chants and gestures by its supporters. Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada were also hit with bans and fines, as was Roberto Ayala, a member of Argentina’s coaching team. In a statement, AFA said FIFA’s appeals body had rejected their complaint against the sanctions handed out to Paredes and the association, but had reduced Molina’s punishment from a seven-match ban and $90,000 fine to four games and $60,000. He asked the President to state how many Nigerians had been lifted out of poverty, how many out-of-school children had returned to school and how many functional primary healthcare centres had been built. Obi also questioned the improvement in electricity supply, recalling Tinubu’s earlier promise that Nigerians should not vote for him if his administration failed to fix the power sector. On insecurity, he said Nigerians deserved an explanation of what the government had done to secure the country, which he noted still ranks among the world’s most terrorised countries. “Mr President, Nigerians deserve answers. He added that the New Nigeria he seeks to build would be founded on accountability, transparency and the measurable impact of public resources on citizens. Tinubu had on Friday told supporters at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, that he would spend the night in Akwa Ibom, describing it as a “second term presidential sleep” and expressing confidence in securing re-election in 2027. nigeria.title: Ebola: DRC records 10,668 cases, 5,198 deaths — WHO
nigeria.description: The disease, Bundibugyo virus disease, with transmission continuing across eight provinces, the World Health Organization (WHO) says. The WHO said in a statement on Saturday that the figure recorded was as of Nov. 3, representing a case fatality ratio of 48.7 percent. It said the outbreak had spread geographically, with active transmission ongoing in 51 of the 67 affected health zones across eight provinces. According to WHO, although some areas have recorded a slight decline in cases, sustained and high-level transmission continues across DRC. The organization said 512 deaths had been reported since Oct. 21, comprising 335 deaths in communities and 177 in treatment centers. It expressed concern over the high number of community deaths, particularly among young children, attributing the trend to challenges in early detection and timely access to appropriate healthcare. “No new cases had been reported in Kenya and Nigeria since its previous Disease Outbreak News published on Oct. 23. “However, there is the need for sustained regional preparedness, including cross-border surveillance, monitoring at points of entry, early case detection, and coordinated response measures,” it said. The organization also disclosed that Switzerland and the United Kingdom had medically evacuated confirmed cases involving their citizens, although no new country had reported cases since the previous update. WHO advised against imposing travel or trade restrictions on countries experiencing or responding to the outbreak, based on currently available information. nigeria.title: Oyo’ll no longer depend on oil, raw materials for economic prosperity – Makinde
nigeria.description: …state targets global market for arts, crafts By Adeola Badru The Oyo State Government has declared its determination to move beyond dependence on conventional sources of revenue by harnessing the economic potential of arts, crafts, cultural festivals, and tourism to generate foreign exchange, attract international investments, and create employment opportunities. The government said it was working to transform Nigeria’s rich cultural heritage into commercially viable products for the global export market, positioning the creative economy as a major driver of economic growth and sustainable development. The initiative, which sought to unlock the enormous economic value of indigenous artistic expressions, traditional knowledge, and cultural assets, will be driven through the Oyo State Business Forum 2026, with the theme “Investment and Export Promotion of Arts and Crafts Business in Oyo State.” The forum is expected to bring together investors, artists, craftsmen, exporters, policymakers, and development partners to explore investment opportunities, strengthen export capacity, and expand the international market for Nigerian arts and crafts. Speaking at a press briefing to announce the forum, the Commissioner for Culture and Tourism, Dr. Wasiu Olatubosun, said the administration of Governor Seyi Makinde was deliberately repositioning culture beyond its traditional function as a custodian of heritage to become a productive economic sector capable of generating wealth, attracting investments, and contributing meaningfully to national development. Olatubosun, who spoke at the briefing organized in collaboration with the Oyo State Investment and Public-Private Partnership Agency (OYSIPA) at the state Secretariat, Ibadan, described Nigeria’s cultural wealth as an enormous but largely untapped economic resource that could compete favorably in the international marketplace. He maintained that traditional festivals, indigenous knowledge, artistic expressions, and locally produced crafts possessed considerable commercial value and could become major export commodities if properly researched, documented, developed, and marketed. According to him, the state government is also repositioning its cultural festivals from routine annual celebrations into internationally competitive tourism and entertainment products capable of attracting foreign visitors, investors, and members of the African diaspora. He identified the recent inscription of the Sango Festival on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity as a major boost to Oyo State’s international cultural standing and an opportunity to attract greater global attention. The commissioner explained that the recognition had taken the annual festival in Oyo Town beyond its traditional geographical and cultural boundaries, making it an increasingly attractive destination for international tourists, cultural enthusiasts, and media organizations from Africa, Europe, and the Americas.

nigeria.title: UK Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch says Trump deserved midterm defeat
nigeria.description: British Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has said United States President Donald Trump deserved to be defeated in the midterm elections, describing the setback as “entirely self-inflicted.” In an interview with The Independent , Badenoch criticised Trump’s handling of the Iran war, his trade policies and his treatment of allies. She said his approach did not reflect conservative principles. The Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday’s midterms, flipping at least seven Senate seats and more than two dozen House districts in a major blow to Trump’s Republican Party. Asked whether Trump deserved the defeat, Badenoch replied: “Yeah. He has not been acting in the way that I would consider conservative.” She condemned his tariffs, threats towards Canada and Greenland, and disputes with allies, saying they contradicted the conservative emphasis on free markets and better trade. “Where is the push for free markets and better trade… rather than protectionism, America first, the squabbling with allies? That’s not what conservatives do,” she said. Badenoch also criticised Trump’s personal attacks on journalists and political figures, stating that his conduct fell short of the standards expected of a statesman. “Trump is very charming in person, but you see the way that he talks about journalists, about individuals. It doesn’t meet the standards a statesman should meet – always wanting to get dirty in terms of insults and so on,” she said. She expressed particular unhappiness with Trump’s remarks about British Prime Minister Keir Starmer and described his treatment of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at the White House as “awful.” On the Iran conflict, Badenoch said she understood and supported Trump’s initial decision to take military action due to concerns about Iran acquiring nuclear weapons, but questioned the lack of a clear strategy. “We don’t want them getting nuclear weapons. But where’s the plan?” she asked. Badenoch added that she would have been content if Trump had lost the 2024 presidential election to Kamala Harris. When asked which of the two candidates she preferred, she said: “I would say I like them both equally. Make of that what you will.” She further argued that Trump had squandered the broad coalition of voters that helped him win the presidency, including increased support from Latino and Black voters. “What’s the first thing he does? Tariffs, and then talking about Greenland and Canada. A lot of people were wondering, ‘What are you doing?’” she said. Badenoch became leader of the UK Conservative Party and Leader of the Opposition in November 2024. Born Olukemi Olufunto Adegoke in London in 1980 to Nigerian parents, she previously served as Business and Trade Secretary under former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak. nigeria.title: Okafor strike for Leeds ends Tottenham’s winning run
nigeria.description: Leeds rode their luck to beat in-form Tottenham 1-0 on Saturday, benefiting from a controversial decision to allow Jayden Bogle to stay on the pitch after an ugly tackle on Mathys Tel. Substitute Noah Okafor was the match-winner, making an almost immediate impact after being introduced by Leeds boss Daniel Farke in the 77th minute. The home team started brightly and Spurs breathed a sigh of relief in the early minutes when VAR ruled that Mateus Fernandes had not handled the ball in the penalty area. As the first half wore on the visitors established themselves, though clear chances were at a premium. Leeds got the benefit of a contentious decision about 10 minutes before the break when Bogle caught Tel’s trailing ankle with his studs, leaving the Tottenham winger writhing on the ground in pain. After a lengthy VAR check no action was taken against Bogle, who was not even booked for the challenge, but Tel was forced off a few minutes later, hobbling off to be replaced by Dominic Solanke. Leeds had two big chances early in the second half as Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s header was blocked by Solanke before Nico Elvedi nodded wide on the follow-up. Calvert-Lewin then burst forward again but opted to pass to Ao Tanaka rather than shooting and the Japanese international skied his shot. Leeds were now on the front foot and Antonin Kinsky produced a wonderful stop after Sean Longstaff’s swivel and shot. But they got the goal their pressure deserved in the 79th minute. Harry Wilson, another substitute, controlled the ball and played it into the path of Okafor, who gave Kinsky no chance. Spurs came agonisingly close to an equaliser but goalkeeper James Trafford made a brilliant save from Jan Paul van Hecke’s header. The result ends Tottenham’s run of three straight league wins while it was the first victory in six games for Leeds, who climbed to eighth in the table. nigeria.title: 2027: Collect campaign money, but vote your conscience, Makinde tells Nigerians

business.title: U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi

For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. sports.description: SEATTLE — Penn State football appears to be getting healthy at most every place on its roster for the stretch drive, in order to best save whatever it can of a second straight disappointing season. Rather, the Lions and quarterback Rocco Becht may lean, again, on their tight end room that finally appears fully healthy, particularly standout blocker and possession receiver Gabe Burkle, who has been working his way back from knee surgery last fall. Otherwise, the Lions appear in better shape, physically, for Washington and the final three games than they have for most of the season. Penn State's list of unavailable players for the Washington game includes Howard, linebacker Alex Tatsch, defensive end Max Granville , cornerback Tyler Armstead, defensive tackle Alijah Carnell and kickoff specialist Cristiano Rosa . sports.description: Captain Sione Tuipulotu took responsibility for Scotland's second-half Nations Championship collapse against New Zealand, saying they were "nowhere near accurate enough". Trailing by just three points at half-time, Scotland were well in the contest as they sought a first victory against the All Blacks at the 34th attempt. However, they failed to score any points in the second half as New Zealand swept to a clinical 43-21 victory at Murrayfield. Tuipulotu was sin-binned on 50 minutes after a succession of penalties went against the Scots and they were unable to wrestle back momentum from there. "Disappointing," was Tuipulotu's one-word review post-match. He added: "We played our rugby in the first half but we probably left points out there. We were nowhere near accurate enough second half, and we couldn't stick with them, it's really disappointing. "Our discipline wasn't good enough, and it starts with me. I don’t really care about highlights or anything like that. I do what my team needs to win, whether that’s just playing defense, getting steals, getting blocks, or pushing in transition. I’m one of those girls that a coach will love to coach, because I don’t really care about the highlight reel and stuff like that. I just want to do what the team needs to do to win.” Rutgers was one of the more recent teams to enter her recruitment, but her relationships with the staff were central. “Rutgers has been on me a lot too, just because they’re literally an hour away from me,” she previously told Rivals. “It’s been really good. Coach G[ary Redus] met most of my family. He was recruiting me at LSU, so I talked to him a lot. I also talk a lot with Lauren Hansen. She used to play for Exodus and she coaches for Exodus for a little bit too, so I already had that bond with her and it’s great talking to them. My parents love him and he’s a great guy. He loves to talk. Campus is beautiful too.” There were several factors that went into her decision. “A connection with the coaches,” she said of important factors. “I’d say play style, like how I’d fit in the system and making sure I get a good opportunity to play. I also have an older sister and I want to make sure that she’s able to come with me. Also somewhere that I can develop. I want to make it to the league.”

sports.title: Swans boss Matos defends Stamenic over red card
sports.description: Swansea had been the more threatening side at Birmingham until Marko Stamenic (right) was sent off [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Vitor Matos has defended Marko Stamenic after the midfielder was sent off during Swansea City's defeat at Birmingham City. Stamenic saw red in the 26th minute for a heavy challenge on Ethan Laird. Birmingham seized the initiative after Stamenic's early exit, with Jay Stansfield swiftly putting the Blues ahead and then netting a late winner after Swansea levelled in the second half. Matos suggested Stamenic should not have been dismissed because he played the ball rather than former Swansea loanee Laird. "I cannot change what the referee decided," said the Swansea head coach. "I think what happened in that situation was that Marko touched the ball. He tackled the ball with the first foot, he tackled the ball with the second foot. "There's no contact between the two players, so then it's the judgement of the ref if that's a red or not. It's up to him not me." Birmingham beat 10-man Swansea to go top of table Stamenic faces a three-match ban after the first sending off of his Swansea career, with Birmingham boss Chris Davies describing the red card incident as "a poor challenge". Unless Swansea launch a successful appeal, New Zealand player Stamenic will miss games against West Brom, Middlesbrough and Cardiff City after the upcoming international break. "I am here already [in English football] for a good amount of time - I was here before," Matos added. "I saw so many challenges worse than this in the last game. Some of these challenges end up with players injured. It's just harsh when we have this challenge and then there's a red card. "It's for the refs to judge and try to find an agreement on where the line is." He pointed to a 5 percent rise in track admissions and a 12 percent jump in kids under 12 showing up to races, per Newsday . The sport is shifting its focus from the couch to the digital feed, betting that new fans will find the action online first. This is a bold gamble for a league built on tradition, but the numbers back the move. Digital First Strategy O’Donnell knows that a fan in New York or Seattle cannot drive to a race every weekend. The solution is to meet them where they live. “If you’re in New York or you’re in Seattle, and you don’t have a race, what is that entry point?,” O’Donnell said Friday. The answer is short clips and influencer content. To expand the series past its southern origins and enter international markets, the sanctioning body is leveraging YouTube and social media influencers. This strategy acknowledges that the path to a ticket starts with a viral moment on a phone screen. While critics might focus on the drop in broadcast viewership, the CEO sees a different picture. NBC viewership for last week’s Cup race at Martinsville Speedway was down 15 percent from last year, according to Newsday. With an average of just under 2 million viewers, that event became the least-watched non-delayed Cup race on broadcast television. The league is also celebrating the addition of Dodge as a fourth manufacturer, adding more competition and buzz to the garage. sports.title: Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton set for blockbuster rematch in final of Paris Masters
sports.description: Carlos Alcaraz set up a rematch with US Open conqueror Ben Shelton after he eased into a maiden Paris Masters final with a 6-4 6-4 victory over Casper Ruud . Seven-time grand slam champion Alcaraz lost out in an epic to Shelton at Flushing Meadow in September on his comeback from a four-month lay-off with a wrist injury. The world number three has returned to the winners’ circle twice since his exit in the early hours in New York, but will aim to gain revenge on Shelton and secure another ATP 1000 title on Sunday. US Open runner-up Shelton got the better of home favourite Luca Van Assche by a 5-7 6-3 6-4 score at the start of the day. Carlos Alcaraz set up a meeting with Ben Shelton after a straight set win over Casper Ruud in Paris (Getty) After Shelton’s two-hour-and-17-minute battle, all eyes in Paris were on Alcaraz, who saved two match points to defeat Taylor Fritz on Friday. Ruud narrowly held off Alcaraz in two of his first three service games before the Spaniard broke to move 4-3 up and closed out the first set with a 130mph ace. The second stayed on serve until Alcaraz picked the opportune moment to break to go 5-4 ahead and secured victory inside 97 minutes. It made it eight wins in a row for Alcaraz, who reached an 11th Masters final, but first in Paris. Ben Shelton defeated Luca van Assche to reach Paris Masters Open (Reuters) “This tournament has always been really tough for me. I’ve struggled every time,” Alcaraz said on court. “I’ve come into this part of the season much fresher, hungry, ambitious, excited about coming to the tournaments and stepping on the court, playing matches and competing. I’m just really happy that I made the final.” Shelton, meanwhile, reached the final when he rallied from a break down in the deciding set to beat Van Assche on Saturday. The third-seeded American looked in trouble when the unseeded Frenchman broke his serve for a 3-1 lead in the third set. But Shelton responded by winning the next four games to lead 5-3. “I know there is always going to be some little chance I can execute,” Shelton said. “If I can be brave and keep winning my serve and stick with the guy, I feel there is a small window.”

sports.description: Motorsport photo There were options for John Hunter Nemechek to remain in the NASCAR Cup Series in some capacity after his surprise dismissal from Legacy Motor Club but he is more focused on winning races right now. Thus, his joining Haas Factory Team for the 2027 O’Reilly Series championship, in a move that checks a lot of boxes for every party involved. It’s been kind of a turbulent year for the second-generation racer who signed an extension with Legacy, announced in May at Texas Motor Speedway, which was then rescinded in September when Josh Berry was made available. “It's a tough spot to be in, in my opinion, but at the same time from everything that Jimmie (Johnson) and Cal (Wells) have said to me internally, but also publicly to the media and things like that, making sure I’m taken care of next year and honoring my contract through that,” Nemechek said during a press conference on Saturday at Homestead. He hopes to remain friends with Johnson and Wells but he is also no doubt entitled to some form of contract buyout given that they agreed to terms that were ultimately rescinded. “Working through that,” Nemechek said. Haas Factory Team president Joe Custer articulated it as Nemechek ‘dropped into our laps’ because of all the things the 11-race NOAPS and 13-time Truck Series race winner brings to their program. Beyond a track record of success, the relationship with primary sponsor Pye-Barker Fire & Safety means a great deal to HFT as well. “Pye-Barker, a lot of their customers are in the manufacturing sector, and that's what Haas Automation does,” Custer said. “We own the manufacturing sector in this sport.” Haas’ CNC machine business and customer car program are just two examples of how vital it is in the NASCAR industry. “We're excited because there's a hundred thousand Haas customers that are potential fits for Pye-Barker,” Custer said. “So there is a B2B play and we're going to work hard. sports.title: Toto Wolff doesn’t think Kimi Antonelli “would have lasted in other teams”
sports.description: Motorsport photo Formula 1 is a vicious meat grinder for young talent. If a rookie doesn't perform immediately, there is usually a very short leash before a team principal shows them the door. For Mercedes , taking a massive gamble on teenager Andrea Kimi Antonelli to replace Lewis Hamilton was the ultimate risk. And as team boss Toto Wolff freely admits, there was a dark stretch during the Italian's 2025 rookie campaign where almost any other team on the grid would have pulled the plug. Speaking to Sky Sports F1’s Naomi Schiff and Simon Lazenby following Free Practice 3 at the Brazilian Grand Prix, Wolff took a moment to reflect on exactly how close his newly crowned world champion came to the brink. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Before Antonelli hoisted the 2026 championship trophy in Mexico City, he had to survive a nightmare slump. "What I'm particularly proud of is that I don't think he would have lasted in other teams after an F2 season, which wasn't overwhelming," Wolff confessed on the Sky broadcast. "And this spell of nine races without any points last year." The Mercedes shield When the pressure was at its absolute peak, and critics were questioning the factory seat, the Brackley squad closed ranks. They ignored the outside noise and looked at the telemetry. "We just trusted our data, trusted our feeling about the personality and the potential," Wolff explained. "Because there's so many that came out and said, what a talent. And that wasn't the journey." Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes Instead of letting the then-19-year-old drown in the immense pressure of the Silver Arrows spotlight, Wolff and his senior leadership team built a psychological fortress around him. They gave him the time that other teams simply refuse to offer. "The journey was developing the talent, nurturing, mentoring, shielding him, protecting him," Wolff noted. "And eventually, you know, he in the car is just delivered absolutely amazingly." The ultimate vindication arrived in Mexico when Antonelli secured the crown. Wolff's patience didn't just save a generational talent from being destroyed by the F1 machine - it built the youngest world champion in F1 history. Ferguson told The Register in an interview that while Fireworks AI, a managed inference provider, supports on-prem AI, "we're trying to push people more and more away from it because frankly, it's just the economics." The GPU hardware is just so expensive that if you can't keep it fully utilized, it's a waste of money, he contends. Ten thousand GPUs, he said, represent a billion dollars of capital. "You don't want those things to be sitting idle," he said. For companies with particularly sensitive workloads, Ferguson said, Fireworks is happy to work something out – it offers a service called Sovereign for just that purpose and it has partners like Microsoft that can help. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments." science.title: Star Wars is experiencing a golden age of video games
science.description: After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games . With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
science.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. science.title: What's that bright 'star' in the early morning sky? It's not a star at all!
science.description: null Early morning risers heading to work or school before sunrise are likely to notice a very bright, star-like object appearing low in the east-southeast sky just before sunrise. What is somewhat amazing is that just a couple of weeks ago this object wasn't there at all, but now it literally stands out with such brilliance as to almost command the attention of commuters who might be traveling in an easterly direction to "Look at me!" The object in question is, of course, the planet Venus, which is currently amid one of its most spectacular forays into the morning sky, literally "vaulting up" into prominence. On Oct. 24, Venus came to inferior conjunction, passing between the Earth and sun and shifting from the evening into the morning sky. And the view is only going to get better in the days and weeks to come! Ascending in the morning In terms of morning visibility, Venus is now in a literal and figurative sense "rising to the occasion." It's now rising before the break of dawn, more than 90 minutes before sunrise. From here on, it will rise three minutes earlier each day, so that by Dec. 17 it will rise 3 hours and 50 minutes before sunrise and blaze in a completely dark sky for more than two hours before the first vestige of morning twilight. It will reach peak brilliance on Nov. 29, when it will shine at an eye-popping magnitude of -4.9. That's 12 times brighter than its nearest planetary competitor, Jupiter and a full 25 times more dazzling than Sirius, the brightest of all stars. If you live in a rural location with no light pollution to interfere, you might be able to make out that it is casting a visible shadow and if you follow it right on through sunrise, it will be evident to your naked eye in full daylight: a tiny white speck plainly evident against the blue daytime sky. In a way, we could even regard Venus as this year's version of a "Christmas Star," glowing with stunning radiance ". . . in the east" like the biblical quote mentioned in St. Matthew. What goes up, must come down After reaching its high point in terms of morning visibility in mid-December, Venus will start a long, slow slide back toward the sun, rising about 1½ minutes later each morning from New Year's Day through late March. By then, Venus will be coming up as dawn is breaking, roughly 100 minutes before sunrise. Venus will continue to get gradually lower and rise progressively later during the spring and by late June it will be coming up less than an hour before sunrise, ultimately vanishing into the bright dawn twilight by July. Venus will then go on a "summer sabbatical" of sorts and will not reappear again until about this time next year when it will begin a very fine evening apparition. So, if any of your friends or relatives remark to you that they saw a "strange UFO" on the way to work or school recently, you now can set them straight. It's not E.T. It's only Venus. science.title: Record-breaking, fast-spinning magnet could help uncover new physics
science.description: Magnets can be made to levitate by the Meissner effect Science History Images / Alamy A tiny magnet that levitates within a superconductor trap may be the fastest spinning object visible to the naked eye, and one of the fastest spinning objects ever made. In the future, it could be used in experiments searching for mysterious dark matter particles and aid the development of quantum technologies. Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with perfect efficiency, and they also expel any magnetic field that tries to permeate them – a phenomenon known as the Meissner effect. Because of this, a magnet placed above a superconductor experiences repulsive magnetic forces and starts to levitate. Tao Wang at the Agency for Science Technology and Research in Singapore and his colleagues have now set one such levitating magnet spinning at an unprecedently fast rate. Read more A miniature magnet rivals behemoths in strength for the first time The researchers used a spherical magnet made from neodymium, iron and boron that was about 30 micrometres wide, similar to the width of a fine human hair. They placed it in a cylindrical container made from lead, then enclosed that container in a chamber devoid of air, or a vacuum chamber. Advertisement Next, they used liquid helium to cool the whole setup to approximately -269°C (-452°F), only a few degrees above the coldest possible temperature . Under these extreme circumstances, lead behaved as a superconductor and the lack of air meant that the magnet could levitate within it without bumping into any particles. The team set the magnet spinning with a magnetic coil, ultimately pushing this tiny rotor to 138 million revolutions per minute. Wang says the magnet’s spinning was also very stable: it would take 17 days for its spinning speed to decrease by 50 per cent, something that would typically happen more quickly due to interactions between the magnet and its environment. “In terms of how many turns it makes before slowing down significantly, this is in the same league as the Earth’s spinning,” he says. “This, so far, is the fastest magnetically levitated rotor.” The record for the fastest rotating human-made object is also held by a levitated sphere, but that one was nano-sized, so invisible to the naked eye, and levitated by laser beams. Wang says this could be useful for builders of quantum computers, which often must be kept extremely cold and isolated in order to work. Heatwaves across the world have shocked scientists with their scale and severity in recent years, with heat extremes dramatically outstripping both historical records and the predictions of climate models. Read more Extreme heat is now making cities unlivable. How can we survive it? In the UK in 2022, temperatures exceeded 40°C (104 ° F) for the first time in history, despite predictions that such a milestone was probably still years away. Likewise, the 2021 heatwave in the Pacific Northwest saw temperatures hit extremes that far outstripped climate model projections. One team thinks the answer lies partly in the soil. Scientists already knew that high-pressure systems allow more solar radiation to reach Earth’s surface, heating up the land.
